agenda.title: The module split: what behaviour each of slots A-D owns, now (wave 1) and as later waves add references, functions, recalculation and cycles; which slot each builder owns
The interfaces: every exported function with its arguments and results, how values and errors are represented, how modules import each other (relative paths), and who writes ARCH.md

args.title: ARCH: the design as decided
args.accept: live/bench5/work/ARCH/ARCH.md: the kickoff's decisions (MTG-1 minutes) as the contract. For each slot A-D a section '## Slot X: <file>.mjs' with a line 'exports: <name>, <name>' then the signature and behaviour of each export, what the slot owns across the waves, and its owner; a section on SHEET (live/bench5/work/SHEET/sheet.mjs, createSheet) saying how it uses the slots; the import paths (../MOD-X/<file>.mjs). Plus one arch.test.mjs that checks ARCH.md has all four slots.

args.title: MOD-A: the module in slot A
args.accept: live/bench5/work/MOD-A/<the file ARCH.md names for slot A>, with exactly the exports and behaviour ARCH.md gives slot A, for every wave released so far (live/bench5/SPEC5.md), plus your own *.test.mjs in the same folder.

args.title: SHEET: the integrated sheet
args.accept: live/bench5/work/SHEET/sheet.mjs exporting createSheet() as live/bench5/SPEC5.md describes it, for every wave released so far, built only from the slot modules as ARCH.md wires them, plus your own sheet.test.mjs. The hidden acceptance tests run on this sheet and report failing categories: when one is in another slot's module, raise it with the lead.
